contribution_types.scope: Main conference, long and short papers
contribution_types.quote: long and short papers featuring substantial, original, and unpublished research

contribution_types.scope: ACL 2025 special theme track, long or short papers
contribution_types.quote: The theme track submissions can be either long or short.

review_criteria.name: Scope covers all aspects of CL and NLP
review_criteria.official_explanation: The call states the conference scope for submitted work.
review_criteria.quote: invites the submission of long and short papers featuring substantial, original, and unpublished research in all aspects of Computational Linguistics and Natural Language Processing

review_criteria.name: Substantial, original, unpublished research
review_criteria.official_explanation: Originality and non-publication are stated conditions of a submission.
review_criteria.quote: long and short papers featuring substantial, original, and unpublished research

review_criteria.name: Several contribution shapes are in scope
review_criteria.official_explanation: The call lists non-standard contribution shapes that are explicitly in scope.
review_criteria.quote: papers may contribute negative findings, survey an area, announce the creation of a new resource, argue a position, report novel linguistic insights derived using existing computational techniques, and reproduce, or fail to reproduce, previous results

review_criteria.name: Two-way anonymized, double-blind review
review_criteria.official_explanation: The review process is stated to be double-blind on the ARR side.
review_criteria.quote: The reviewing process will continue to be double-blind. Reviewers will not see authors, nor will authors see reviewers, and reviews on ARR will not be made publicly visible.

review_criteria.name: Accepted papers must be presented
review_criteria.official_explanation: Presentation is a condition for appearing in the proceedings.
review_criteria.quote: All accepted papers must be presented at the conference to appear in the proceedings.

review_criteria.name: Two-stage review: ARR review then conference decision
review_criteria.official_explanation: Review is delegated to ARR; acceptance decisions are made at the conference.
review_criteria.quote: Authors submit articles to ARR, where submissions receive reviews and meta-reviews from ARR reviewers and action editors;

mandatory_policy.statement: ACL 2025 reviews submissions through ACL Rolling Review; the conference makes the final decisions.
mandatory_policy.quote: ACL 2025 will use ACL Rolling Review (ARR) as a reviewing system, but final decisions will be made by the conference.

mandatory_policy.statement: Long and short submissions must follow all ARR submission requirements, including 8-page long and 4-page short limits, two-way anonymization, the ethics checklist and a Limitations section.
mandatory_policy.quote: Both long and short paper submissions should follow all of the ARR submission requirements , including: Long Papers (8 pages) and Short Papers (4 pages) Instructions for Two-Way Anonymized Review Authorship Citation and Comparison Multiple Submission Policy , Resubmission Policy , and Withdrawal Policy Ethics Policy including the responsible NLP research checklist Limitations Paper Submission and Templates Optional Supplementary Materials

mandatory_policy.statement: At ARR submission, authors must specify which co-authors commit to covering reviewing in the cycle.
mandatory_policy.quote: During the ARR submission process, authors will be required to specify which co-authors are committing to cover reviewing in this reviewing cycle.

mandatory_policy.statement: Accepted papers must be presented at the conference to appear in the proceedings.
mandatory_policy.quote: All accepted papers must be presented at the conference to appear in the proceedings.

mandatory_policy.statement: All ACL 2025 deadlines are at 11:59PM UTC-12:00, anywhere on Earth.
mandatory_policy.quote: Note: All deadlines are at 11:59PM UTC-12:00 (“anywhere on Earth”).

recommended_practice.statement: The theme track invited empirical and theoretical research and position and survey papers on the Generalization of NLP Models.
recommended_practice.quote: The theme track invites empirical and theoretical research and position and survey papers reflecting on the Generalization of NLP Models.

recommended_practice.statement: There is no anonymity period requirement; per the ACL and ARR policies authors may post or discuss non-anonymous preprints while under review.
recommended_practice.quote: Following the ACL and ARR policies , there is no anonymity period requirement.

recommended_practice.statement: Committing to ACL 2025 is optional regardless of the preferred venue declared at ARR submission.
recommended_practice.quote: Authors who selected ACL 2025 as a preferred venue when submitting to ARR may choose not to commit to ACL 2025 after receiving their reviews, and authors who selected a preferred venue other than ACL 2025 when submitting to ARR are still welcome to commit to ACL 2025.

compliance_checks.requirement: Submission follows the ARR submission requirements, which include a Limitations section and the responsible NLP research checklist.
Long paper content is at most 8 pages; short paper content is at most 4 pages.
Two-way anonymized review: no author names or affiliations.
Ethics policy and responsible NLP research checklist submitted as required by the ARR submission requirements.
Confirm the submitted paper matches the current ARR submission requirements that the ACL 2025 call incorporates by reference.

changes_from_prior_year.change: ACL 2025 announces a new special theme track: “Generalization of NLP Models”.
Policy differences between ACL 2024 and ACL 2025 are not asserted; no ACL 2024 document was retrieved and rules are not inherited across years.

unknown_policies.question: Which ARR rules were mandatory for an ACL 2025 submission?
unknown_policies.reason: The ACL 2025 call incorporates the ARR submission requirements by reference instead of restating them; those rules belong to the ARR profiles for the cycle concerned and are not reproduced here as ACL mandatory policy.

unknown_policies.question: Is there a separate ACL 2025 Findings policy?
unknown_policies.reason: The call states that papers not selected for the main conference will automatically be considered for Findings, but no separate Findings policy page was retrieved.

unknown_policies.question: Does this profile still describe current practice?
unknown_policies.reason: ACL 2025 is a past edition; the profile records only what the 2025 documents govern and must not be inherited by later editions.
